items.title: Brownout is never a rational choice with homogeneous towers
items.why: N towers at 60% fire rate = 0.6N effective; with a slot-limited board that is always worse than running capacity/draw at full rate. Brownout only becomes a tradeoff with heterogeneous draws (e.g. briefly raising a 40MW shield wall). Verify this holds once anchor-04 unlocks shield-wall.

items.title: Editor preview shows flat-colour tiles until the project is reloaded, because the Sprites autoload is only instantiated in-editor at startup
items.note: anchor_view._sprite_lib() builds its own sprites.gd instance when the autoload is absent, which is the editor case. sprites.gd's manifest load moved from _ready() into load_library() so it can be called explicitly — the same fix anchor_data.gd already makes for Content. items.title: HUD and dialog build their Control widgets in code rather than being authored in the scene
items.note: Superseded by decision 043. Every HUD panel is now sized from content — build grid from the unlock count, inspector from the tallest datasheet measured against the font's line height, threat panel from the busiest wave. A .tscn cannot express those heights, so authoring it would mean keeping all the layout code and adding a scene that disagrees with it. Two sources of truth for one geometry.

items.title: Sprite pivot ignores the render camera height_bias, so every sprite draws ~48px above its tile
items.why: Hover highlight and turrets sit off their slot rings. Manifest pivot is (128,128); measured tile silhouette centre is (127.5,176.5). render_pair uses height_bias=0.55 but _measure_tile calibrates at 0.0, so the bias never reaches the pivot

items.why: Two identical --autoplay runs reached different sim states at frame 1800 (coverage 0.306 vs 0.394, wave 6 vs wave 1). Makes screenshot-based art review unreliable; suspect the minf(delta,0.25) clamp absorbing a long first frame

items.title: Sim state diverged twice at a fixed frame while the sprite import cache was stale
items.why: Observed twice (wave 6 vs wave 1 at frame 1800) in runs made after re-rendering but before 'Godot --headless --path . --import'. NOT reproducible since: 12/12 runs now identical, including under CPU load. main.gd now prints STATE frame/sim_t/wave/phase on every --shot, so a recurrence is self-evident rather than inferred from pixels. items.title: Shield wall is overpriced: 40 MW for a 0.45x slow in radius 2.0 is never worth building
items.why: Measured under decision 022 at anchor-04: no-wall wins 10/9/6 lives, wall-always-on loses hard and brutal, optimally-toggled wall loses brutal. Its 40 MW is a 42% overdraw pricing at 62.5%. Either the draw comes down or the effect becomes decisive

items.title: Ion lance is strictly dominated: worse damage per megawatt than the pulse turret even against armour
items.why: Measured: vs plate-4 the lance does 18.3 dps on 34 MW (0.54 per MW), the pulse turret 6.7 dps on 12 MW (0.56 per MW). The designated anti-armour unlock is worse at armour than the starter gun, while costing 3x the funds and draw so it buys fewer emplacements covering less path. Same class as LF-032. Raising damage to 66 fixes brutal but hard still grades single-solution

items.title: Act II waves are thin (2-5 units per type) and lives run high (16-24) because shielded heavies and drain eat the whole difficulty budget — consider a mid-cost anti-armour emplacement or a lance/mortar draw cut so volume can come back
items.note: Half solved by decision 044: the cause was the sweep's scorer, not the content. It scored clean cells by distinct winning builds alone, so more lives always scored higher and the loosest cell always won. Robustness is now a threshold (ROBUST_ENOUGH=8), with density and tightness deciding beyond it. Seven anchors tightened — 18/19 from 30 lives to 22, 22 from 32 to 26, 24 from 44 to 40; Act III mean 31.8 -> 27.5. Density did NOT move and continues as LF-044.

items.title: Godot warns on every boot that user://progress.json is opened as Defend-Claude but stored as defend-claude — a case mismatch that will not open on a case-sensitive export target
items.note: Not a repo defect. project.godot is config/name="Defend-Claude"; the on-disk user dir is lowercase because it was created under an earlier name, and macOS resolves it case-insensitively. A fresh machine or a case-sensitive export creates Defend-Claude and never mismatches. Local artifact only.

items.title: Window title and export name are "Defend-Claude" (the repo name), not LATTICEFALL — project.godot config/name reaches the player
items.note: config/name is Latticefall. Godot derives user:// from it, so Progress.load_state() adopts a pre-rename save once and prints the path it took. Verified against a real save with anchor-01 cleared: clear survived, second boot did not re-adopt, case-mismatch warning gone. Decision 040.

items.title: debris_settle has no CC0 candidate — OpenGameArt's sound corpus has nothing whose filename reads as falling debris. Needs different queries, --commons, or a recording
items.note: Not sourceable: the entire CC0 sound corpus offers a shovel, a splash and a sand spell for this. Synthesized instead — debris is a stochastic cloud of tiny impacts, which is what synthesis is good at, so decision 009 had it on the wrong side of its own boundary. Rebuilds byte-identical. Plays under warden_death for units of 150 HP or more. Decision 041.

items.title: Act II/III density: decision 047 removed the blocker, now spend it — re-author Act II/III wave composition for more, lighter units at constant wave leak_cost, then re-sweep anchors 09-24
items.note:
PREMISE RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28; the original note was wrong on all three counts.
1. The roster is not the constraint: ~0.52 dps/MW against shielded/armoured vs ~1.0 against plain is a 2x penalty, not an absence. The proposed mid-cost anti-armour emplacement would not have helped.
2. Throughput is not the constraint: 2x damage on every weapon AND +60% capacity (3.2x throughput) still reaches only 1/11 winning builds at weight 1.50 on anchor-20.
3. 'Does not grade clean at any life count' was false — anchor-20 at weight 1.50 grades clean at 72 lives. Never tested: sweep.py defaults to weights [0.85, 1.0, 1.15] and the anchor's current life count.

ROOT CAUSE, now fixed by decision 047: density and leak-tension were the same axis, because a leak cost one life whether it was a 22 hp mote or a 520 hp Column. leak_cost = max(1, round(hp/130)) makes trading one Column for four ~130 hp units tension-neutral.

REMAINING WORK, mechanical and not blocked on the owner: re-author Act II and III wave composition to field more, lighter units in place of the bricks, holding each wave's total leak_cost roughly where it is, then re-sweep anchors 09-24. Judge the result on leak budget (lives / total leak_cost), not on raw lives — Act I sits at 8.7%, Act II 18.0%, Act III 30.4%.

items.title: The instrument column cannot reflow, so interface scale is capped at 125%. content_scale_factor divides the 1920x1080 design space, and the column needs ~847px of height at anchor-24 (nine emplacements, eight reserved datasheet rows) — 150% leaves 720 and clips the SELL/UPGRADE/power controls. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 asks for 200%. Needs a column that can reflow (scroll, collapse the datasheet to the selected tower's rows, or move the build bar out of the column) rather than a larger multiplier

Threat panel shows base enemy HP, not hp * difficulty multiplier — on hard and brutal every unit is understated (hud.gd:597). The panel is the player's whole read on what is coming, so it should show the HP they will actually shoot at

items.title: THREAT_W is hand-derived from the widest trait row in the current roster (hud.gd:60). Nothing recomputes or asserts it, so a future unit with a longer trait line overflows the panel silently

items.title: Hollow lit cones are laterally off-axis from their dark cones, so the emissive collapses at yaw 315. cone() rotates each primitive about its own origin, so two cones sharing rot=(11,-8,0) but sitting at different z have parallel axes offset by ~0.045 world units (~4px): the lit cone pokes out on the +x+y side and hides behind the dark cone from the opposite camera. Measured glow coverage hollow_shard 0.0061 at y315 vs 0.024-0.036 elsewhere; hollow_echo 0.0089 vs 0.042-0.068. Currently latent because anchor_view.gd only ever draws y045 (see the sibling item). Fix is to put the lit cone on the dark cone's rotated axis, or to build both from one origin, and it applies to the whole Hollow set at once rather than shard alone

anchor_view.gd hardcodes yaw 45 for every drawable (drawables(), lines 495 and 508), so 156 of the 208 atlas cells are never drawn. The pipeline renders, masks, packs and imports four yaws per asset and the manifest exposes all four, but nothing picks one from unit heading or tower target. Consequence beyond the wasted 3/4 of the atlas: yaw-only art defects are invisible in game, which is how the Hollow yaw-315 emissive collapse survived unnoticed. Either drive yaw from movement direction, or drop to a single yaw and stop rendering the other three

check_banned_terms() rglobs the whole repo and only exempts docs/NOMENCLATURE.md by exact path, so a git worktree under .claude/worktrees/ carrying its own copy of the bible failed the gate with six false hits. Fixed by skipping .claude alongside .venv, addons and .godot. Kept as a record of the second-order trap it exposed: the backlog itself is scanned, so an item that quotes the terms it is about turns the gate red — the item must describe the hits, never repeat them

Board camera: pan and zoom. Pan on middle-drag plus lf_* keys and edge-scroll, NOT left-drag — left click arms builds and selects emplacements, so drag-to-pan turns every slipped click into a camera move. The board cursor should carry the camera with it, which gives keyboard and gamepad panning without a second system. Zoom transforms the BOARD LAYER ONLY: the HUD ladder and palette were solved for WCAG AA at a known size (045/046) and scaling them with the board silently undoes it. Zoom out is cheap; zoom in past 1.0 softens sprites, which are a fixed 256px atlas at one orthographic scale, so either raise the render base or clamp. Value is inspection on a busy board, not navigation — a 17x13 grid already fits — so it must never be required to play. Needs a --camera x,y,zoom verification hook or every --shot/--a11y report becomes camera-state dependent

standard_policies() cannot express a mixed board: every Policy is a total preference order and _try_build fills every free slot greedily from the top, so a graded build is all-of-one-thing. 'Three pulse turrets in front of an ion lance' is not in the search space, which makes claims like 'the escort brings the cheap emplacements back' unfalsifiable by the harness that is supposed to test them. Needs capped-core policies (cap the expensive tower at N, fill the rest cheap)

PRESSURE_FLOOR in sim/run.py is a dead check: peak load ratio is >=100% of capacity on all 24 anchors x 3 difficulties, and still >=75% everywhere with the greedy-overdraw policy excluded, so 'the player is pressed against capacity' can never fail. Either measure pressure on winning builds only, or raise the floor until it discriminates

anchor_sim._step's splash loop tests 'u == target' but Godot 4.7 compares Dictionary by value (probed: two dicts with equal contents are ==, and Array.find matches by value), while sim/engine.py tests 'u is target'. Two units of the same kind with equal hp and equal dist therefore drop out of splash damage in GDScript and take it in Python. Latent only because same-kind units spawn on different ticks so their dist differs — a wave table that spawns two identical units on the same tick turns it into a parity failure. Found while deciding where facing state could live (LF-050); the fix is an identity-safe test on the GDScript side, e.g. comparing by index
items.note: fixed by comparing target by index; Godot Dictionary == is a value comparison, probed

items.title: Running the editor import (godot --headless --path . --import) rewrote scripts/menu.gd from tab indentation to four-space indentation, a 442-line no-op diff that has to be reverted by hand before committing. Reproduced once in a worktree with no .godot; cause not identified (editor settings or an addon under addons/). Either pin the indentation in .editorconfig for the editor to honour, or stop the import from touching scripts at all

At 200% interface scale the two instrument panels cover nearly the whole board (420+528 of a 960px design space), so the anchor is playable but barely watchable. Consider a hide-panels toggle or a compact threat panel below ~1100px of viewport width

options_menu.gd _fit() sets size on a node with full-rect anchors, which Godot warns about on every boot: 'Nodes with non-equal opposite anchors will have their size overridden after _ready()'. Harmless but it is noise in every run log
scripts/main.gd is indented with 4 spaces while every other .gd file uses tabs. Cosmetic, but it makes a whole-file diff out of any tool that normalises indentation

The gate's rendered checks read display state from the player's save. window_mode, resolution and ui_scale live in user://progress.json, which is outside the repo, so game renders / menu renders / accessibility measured whatever the last person left set — the same tree reported coverage 0.56 and 0.34 on two machines, and the a11y analyser samples its background colours out of those frames. Fixed by leading every rendered check with --display-defaults; kept as the record of why, and because any future verification hook that persists state (the LF-052 board camera especially) has the same hole

The game renders gate check took 2,187,910 ms (36 min) on one run and then PASSED, against 2,493 ms on another run of the same tree the same day. CAUSE, observed by the owner: the three rendered checks launch a REAL Godot window (GL Compatibility reads back nothing headlessly), and macOS throttles a window it considers occluded — cover it, background it, or just keep working in front of it and the frame loop stalls, so main.gd's 'await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw' never resolves. The run does not fail, it waits until the window is visible again and then passes, which is why the gate stayed green. Two mitigations are in: tools/check.py bounds every subprocess (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 300s, PARITY_TIMEOUT 1800s) and reaps grandchildren on timeout, so a stall is now a red run naming the check; and --no-window skips the three windowed checks so the gate is usable while someone is at the machine. Neither is a fix. A real fix makes the capture independent of the compositor presenting frames — candidates: RenderingServer.force_draw() instead of awaiting frame_post_draw, or rendering the shot through a SubViewport. Both need probing against Godot 4.7.1 on this machine, and the occlusion stall has to be reproduced on purpose first (cover the window during a --shot run) or there is no way to tell a fix from a coincidence

The subagent model pin has two holes the agent models gate check cannot see. (1) Built-in agents — Explore, Plan, general-purpose — have no .claude/agents/*.md frontmatter to carry model: sonnet, so they inherit the parent (Opus) unless the model is passed at each call site. Nothing enforces that; it is discipline, and discipline is what failed the first time. (2) The SessionEnd reap hook does not fire when the CLI is killed outright rather than exiting cleanly, so the wrap-skill step is the only real belt and it depends on someone running the wrap. Both are cheap to narrow: a wrapper or documented default for built-in agent calls, and a launchd/login reap or a stale-process check at session start (the start skill now runs reap.py, which covers the common case one session later rather than immediately). Filed because the whole point of decision 051 was replacing remembered rules with mechanical ones, and these two are still remembered rules
